title: Add hot-route protection dashboards + alert rules (enterprise tier + shed reasons)
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes: Adds dashboard + alerting package for Hot-route Capacity Protection: tier-aware traffic/429s, shed reasons, queue-depth signals, and enterprise SLO burn panels.
body: Context: As part of Hot-route Capacity Protection (ENG-4926), SRE needs a consistent set of dashboards + alert rules for protected routes (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank) that make it easy to answer: (1) are enterprise routes staying within SLO under fleet pressure, (2) are we shedding/throttling the right tier first, and (3) what is the reason breakdown (quota vs overload vs admission control) when 429s occur. This PR adds Grafana dashboard definitions (jsonnet) and Prometheus alert rules for the new metrics emitted by gateway/routing/runtime (see redwood PRs for instrumentation and 429 reason codes). Scope: dashboards (per-route/per-tier latency + error + shed), annotations for protection activation events, and paging rules focused on enterprise degradation (not expected best-effort shedding). What’s included: (A) Dashboards: 1) Hot Route Protection – Overview: request volume by route group + tier, 429 rate by reason, shed/admission-control rate, queue depth / scheduler lag signals, and 5xx. 2) Hot Route Protection – Enterprise SLO: p50/p95/p99 latency by protected route group for enterprise tier, availability (2xx/3xx) and error budget burn panels, with burn windows (5m/1h/6h). 3) Hot Route Protection – Debug: top tenants (sampled/low-cardinality) by route group, saturation indicators, and correlation panels for policy-eval latency + routing decision outcomes. (B) Alerts (Prometheus rules): 1) Page: enterprise protected route latency burn > 2x for 15m OR fast burn > 10x for 5m (gated to enterprise tier + protected route groups). 2) Page: enterprise protected route 5xx rate > 1% for 10m (excluding client cancellations). 3) Ticket: sustained overload protection activation (shed_rate_overload_reason > threshold for 30m) when enterprise SLO remains healthy (expected during pressure) to drive capacity follow-up without paging storms. 4) Ticket: missing/flatlined metrics for new overload reason series (helps catch ingestion regressions and the cardinality hotfix class of issues). Notes/guardrails: All queries follow the overload metrics cardinality guidance: no tenant_id in primary panels; we use route_group, tier, region, reason_code only. The “Debug” dashboard includes an opt-in variable for sampled tenant (uses pre-aggregated topK series). Alert rules intentionally avoid paging on best-effort 429 spikes alone; we page only when enterprise SLO signals degrade. Rollout: dashboards are safe to merge before full multi-region enablement; panels will show ‘No data’ until metrics are present. Alert rules are shipped disabled by default via env toggle in the pack; enablement to follow GA checklist (eng-releases thread + canary results). Links: Linear ENG-4926 (dashboards/alerts), ENG-4927 (incident-bot notifications). Related: slo-toolkit PR for standard burn alert helper functions, redwood PR adding overload reason codes to 429s, and runtime PR exporting queue depth + scheduler lag.
changed_areas: README.md (new section: Hot-route protection dashboards + enablement notes)
illustrative_snippets: Alert rule (excerpt): alert: EnterpriseProtectedRouteLatencyBurnFast expr: (slo:burn_rate_5m{service="hosted-api",slo="protected_route_latency",tier="enterprise"} > 10) and on(region) (overload:protection_active{tier="enterprise"} >= 0) for: 5m labels: severity: page annotations: summary: "Fast burn on enterprise protected route latency"
Panel query (excerpt): sum by (region, route_group, tier, reason_code) (rate(api_gateway_requests_total{status="429",route_group=~"protected_.*"}[5m]))

conversation: Allison Grant: Please confirm the tier label source of truth. In some places we used customer_tier in older dashboards. We should standardize on tier to match the metrics standard doc. Also, can we annotate protection activation events on the enterprise SLO dashboard so on-call can correlate quickly?
Sergio Costa (author): Good catch. Updated all queries to tier= (removed customer_tier). Added annotations driven by overload:protection_active transitions (per region + route_group).

Aisha Bello: Paging on 5xx > 1% for 10m seems high/low depending on route; do we have route-specific exceptions? Also, can we gate the paging rule to exclude errors when request volume is tiny (avoid noise in low-traffic regions)?

Sergio Costa (author): Added min_request_rate guard (>= 5 rps aggregate over 10m) and left route-specific thresholds out for now per our goal of low policy complexity. If we need exceptions later, we can add an allowlist by route_group in this pack.

Logan Wright: The debug dashboard includes top tenants — are we sure the query doesn’t accidentally explode series? Please ensure it only hits pre-aggregated topK and doesn’t expose tenant_id by default.
Sergio Costa (author): Adjusted to use overload:top_tenants_by_route_group (pre-aggregated) and made tenant variable empty by default. Added README warning + link to cardinality guidance.

Rafael Mendes: Looks good. Minor: can we rename ‘shed’ panel to ‘admission control / shed’ to match runbook terminology? Also, please add a non-paging alert for missing metrics so we catch ingestion regressions early.
Sergio Costa (author): Done — panel titles updated, and added HotRouteProtectionMetricsMissing as a ticket-level alert.
Aisha Bello: Approved with the min_rps guard.
Rafael Mendes: Approved. Please coordinate enablement with GA checklist.
